notes: 4 greenhouse crops inspired by NASA Veggie and Advanced Plant Habitat experiments on the ISS. Includes real NASA facts and Garden Guide bonus rules.
nasaVeggieFact: In 2015, NASA astronauts aboard the International Space Station harvested and ate the very first space-grown Outredgeous red romaine lettuce from the Veggie chamber using red, blue, and green LED lights!

crops.name: Outredgeous Lettuce
crops.nasaFact: Grown in NASA's ISS Veggie pillow system; fast leafy greens give astronauts fresh crunch and antioxidants.

crops.name: Cherry Belle Radish
crops.nasaFact: In 2020, NASA astronaut Kate Rubins harvested 20 radishes in the Advanced Plant Habitat in just 27 days!

crops.name: Dwarf Space Potato
crops.nasaFact: Potatoes pack high calories per square meter — NASA and CIP tested compact dwarf varieties for future Mars habitats.

crops.name: Dwarf Lima Beans
crops.nasaFact: Legumes fix nitrogen with helpful root microbes and give crews plant-based protein without shipping heavy Earth meat.
